=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py:739-742 | severity=high | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `started_at = time.monotonic()` is captured before the jobs reads, so the jobs reads use up the 55s annotation-read budget. In the worst case (30s timeout, 2s sleep, 30s retry timeout, 62s in all) the loop returns `"unverified"` before it reads any annotation.
  WHY: A final CI run whose jobs read needs the documented one-shot retry is mis-classified as `"unverified"` instead of `"run_cancelled"` and always posts `ci/final=failure`, which is the behaviour the issue asks to suppress. The reviewer rated it MAJOR, mapped here to high.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

- requirement: "otherwise read the run's jobs once (`GET repos/<repo>/actions/runs/<run_id>/jobs?per_page=100&filter=latest`, through `gh_retry`)."
  expected_change_site: scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py `list_run_jobs` / `classify_cancelled_run`
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `list_run_jobs` invokes `gh api` directly with `subprocess.run` (line 512 in `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py`); `classify_cancelled_run` implements its own local one-shot retry (`time.sleep(2)` then call again) at lines 748–751 instead of going through `gh_retry`. No jobs-read path uses the bash `gh_retry` helper, so the issue's rate-limit-aware retry behaviour (wait until reset, up to `GH_RETRY_RATE_LIMIT_MAX_WAIT_SECS`) is not realised. Both reviewers rated it NIT.
- requirement: "reuse the existing classifier in `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py` (reuse it, do not write a second classifier)."
  expected_change_site: scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py — should re-use `classify_runner_shutdown`'s verdict logic, not add a new `classify_cancelled_run` function
  confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The PR adds `classify_cancelled_run` and its CLI wrapper `classify_cancelled_run_cli`, a separate verdict function returning `run_cancelled` / `not_cancelled` / `unverified`. Only the helpers are shared (`list_run_jobs`, `failure_annotations`, `shutdown_only_annotations`, `BENIGN_JOB_CONCLUSIONS`, `CHECK_RUN_URL_PATTERN`, `MAX_FAILED_JOBS_CLASSIFIED`); the verdict logic is written again as a new function. The reviewer rated it NIT.
